 By James Thompson Published on November 16, 2026 Source: Google Street View North Las Vegas Airport was overcast at 63 degrees late Monday morning, and the Las Vegas Valley is forecast to be partly sunny, with highs of 65 to 69 degrees on the west side and 69 to 72 on the east side. Showers remain possible this afternoon, with rain and a slight chance of thunderstorms expected tonight before a cooler, windier Tuesday. The latest NWS valley forecast and airport observation give the updated conditions.
 The latest forecast gives the valley a 20% chance of rain showers this afternoon, then a 70% chance of precipitation tonight, with rain showers likely after midnight and only a slight chance of thunderstorms. Hoodline's Sunday forecast had also flagged unsettled weather and rain chances across the valley. The NWS forecast has the updated timing and probabilities.
 Monday Night Brings The Wettest Stretch
 Clouds will thicken through the evening before showers develop; rain showers are likely after midnight, with only a slight chance of thunderstorms. Lows are forecast at 49 to 53 degrees on the west side of the valley and 53 to 56 on the east side. The NWS valley forecast gives a 70% chance of precipitation tonight.
 The latest outlook puts rainfall at trace amounts to 0.20 inches across most of the region, with 0.25 to 0.60 inches possible in Northeast Clark County, Mohave County and Lincoln County. Even so, wet roads and brief visibility drops could make late-night driving less pleasant, particularly during heavier showers. The NWS says the rain should be spread over time, keeping flood risk on the lower side. 
 The rain forecast is not uniform across the region: the NWS expects the valley’s showers to be light and spread over time, while Northeast Clark County and nearby areas could receive more. That longer, lighter pattern keeps flood risk on the lower side, the forecast office says, though brief downpours could still make roads slick. The latest area forecast discussion puts most of the region at trace amounts to 0.20 inch and higher totals in Northeast Clark, Mohave and Lincoln counties.
 Tuesday Turns Breezy And Cooler
 Tuesday is forecast to be sunny, with highs of 59 to 63 degrees on the west side of the valley and 64 to 67 on the east. Southwest winds of 20 to 30 mph are expected to turn west and ease to 10 to 20 mph in the afternoon. The updated NWS valley forecast gives the latest temperatures and wind timing.
 That combination could make Tuesday feel considerably rougher than Monday, especially for cyclists, motorcyclists and drivers in high-profile vehicles. Loose patio furniture and other lightweight outdoor items may also need securing before the strongest winds arrive.
 Another Rain Chance Arrives Thursday
 Wednesday is forecast to be mostly sunny, with highs of 58 to 62 degrees on the west side of the valley and 62 to 65 on the east. Showers have a 50% chance Wednesday night, followed by likely rain showers Thursday and a 70% chance of precipitation. Thursday highs are forecast at 54 to 58 degrees west and 59 to 62 east. The NWS forecast has the updated midweek timing and temperatures.
 The unsettled pattern also brings a mountain hazard beyond the valley: a Winter Storm Watch covers the Eastern Sierra slopes from late Tuesday night through late Thursday night. The NWS says 10 to 18 inches of snow are possible from 5,000 to 8,000 feet, with 18 to 36 inches above 8,000 feet; its forecast discussion says Mount Charleston could see up to 4 inches. The watch is for the Eastern Sierra slopes , not the Las Vegas Valley.
 The pattern dries out again Friday, when mostly sunny skies and a high near 74 degrees are expected. Highs are forecast near 70 degrees Saturday and 68 degrees Sunday.
